Buyer Added Bid Specific SLA Text Clause(s) OTHER GENERAL CONDITIONS: • The Contractor shall, wherever applicable, obtain and maintain a valid licen

ce the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, read with the applicable Rules, before deploying or engaging contract labour for e xecution of the work under this Contract. The Contractor shall furnish a copy of the valid licence, along with the relevant registration particulars and such other supporting documents as may be required, to the Principal Employer b efore commencement of deployment of contract labour. The Contractor shall not deploy or continue to engage contract labour in circumstances where a valid licence is legally required but has not been o btained or has ceased to be valid. Failure to obtain, maintain or furnish the r equired licence shall constitute a breach of the Contract, entitling the Princip al Employer to take appropriate contractual action, including withholding per mission for deployment, requiring rectification within the permissible period, and initiating termination proceedings in accordance with the terms of the C ontract, without prejudice to any other remedy available under applicable la w. • The Contractor/Service Provider shall ensure timely payment of wages with out any unauthorised deductions within 7 days of the end of the wage period in accordance with the Code on Wages, 2019. • The Contractor shall, at its own cost and expense, provide each contract la bour deployed under this Contract with all necessary Uniform, Shoes, Caps a nd other PPEs whichever are essential as per nature of work and for safety d uring work. Such items shall conform to the applicable statutory requirement s, prescribed safety standards and the safety instructions and requirements of the Principal Employer. The Contractor shall also ensure that every contra ct labour uses the prescribed PPE and safety equipment while performing the assigned duties and complies with all applicable safety rules, procedures and instructions of the Principal Employer. The entire cost of proc urement, provision, maintenance and replacement of PPE, safety equipment and uniforms shall be borne exclusively by the Contractor. The Principal Emp loyer shall not be liable to bear or reimburse any such cost separately. The C ontractor shall accordingly take into account all expenses towards PPE, safet y equipment, uniforms and their maintenance and replacement while quotin g its service charges and other financial components under the Contract. No additional payment, reimbursement or claim on this account shall be admissi ble against the Principal Employer during the currency of the Contract. Any f ailure to comply with this clause shall constitute a breach of the Contract and may attract appropriate contractual action in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Contract, without prejudice to any other rights or remedies available to the Principal Employer under applicable law. • The Contractor shall ensure strict compliance with all applicable provisions of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, the a pplicable Rules, and all safety, health, security and environmental instruction s, procedures and directions issued by the Principal Employer from time to ti me. The Contractor shall be solely responsible for ensuring that all contract l abour deployed under the Contract follows the prescribed safety procedures and uses appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) while performing their assigned duties. The Contractor shall ensure that every contract worker receives appropriate safety induction, job-specific safety training and instruct ions before being assigned any work involving safety risks. The Contractor’s supervisor or authorised representative shall monitor compliance with safety requirements

and shall maintain relevant training, PPE-issue and safety-inspection records for verification by the Principal Employer. • In the event of any breach of safety requirements by the Contractor or its c ontract labour, the Principal Employer shall be entitled to impose the followin g contractual penalties: (a) For a safety violation, a written warning and a penalty of ₹1,000 per occu rrence. (b) For failure to comply with a written safety direction of Principal Employer/ Buyer, a penalty of Rs. 2,000 per occurrence per week. (c) For failure to provide or use mandatory PPE, unauthorised operation of m achinery, bypassing safety guards or permitting work in a hazardous manner , a penalty of Rs. 1,000 per occurrence per week. (d) The applicable penalty shall continue to accrue for each week, or part the reof as specified in the contract, until the Contractor implements the require d corrective measures and the Principal Employer verifies and confirms rectif ication in writing. The imposition of penalty shall not restrict the Principal Em ployer’s right to stop unsafe work, require removal of personnel, or initiate o ther contractual action, including termination in accordance with the contrac t. • The Contractor shall nominate, at its own cost and expense, a competent S upervisor or duly authorized representative for effective supervision, coordin ation and management of the contract labour engaged under this Contract. T he Supervisor/authorized representative shall be responsible for ensuring the attendance, discipline, proper conduct and deployment of contract labour, all ocation and monitoring of assigned duties, compliance with the terms and conditions of t he Contract, and adherence to applicable labour laws, safety rules, security i nstructions and other instructions issued by the Principal Employer from tim e to time. The Supervisor/authorized representative shall also act as the nod al point of contact between the Contractor and the Principal Employer for all matters relating to the deployment and administration of contract labour. Th e Contractor shall furnish the name, contact details and written authorization of the Supervisor/authorized representative to the Principal Employer before commencement of the work. All costs and expenses relating to the deployme nt of the Supervisor/authorized representative shall be borne exclusively by t he Contractor and shall be duly factored into the service charges quoted by t he Contractor. No separate payment or reimbursement on this account shall be admissible from the Principal Employer. • In accordance with Rule 184 of the Occupational Safety, Health and Workin g Conditions (Central) Rules, 2026, read with the applicable provisions of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, the Contrac tor shall nominate one competent and duly authorized representative as a m ember of the Grievance Redressal Committee constituted by the Principal E mployer for redressal of grievances of contract labour deployed under this C ontract. The Contractor shall communicate the name, designation, contact d etails and written authorization of its nominated representative to the Princip al Employer before commencement of deployment of contract labour. The nomination of the Contractor’s representative shall not absolve the Contract or of its statutory or contractual obligations towards contract labour or restri ct the right of any contract labour to seek remedies before the competent au thority in accordance with applicable law.

• The Contractor’s supervisor and contractor’s representative in grievance re dressal committee should not associate with any other firm. • The Contractor shall, at its own cost and without claiming any reimburseme nt from the Principal Employer / Buyer, arrange and ensure the annual health examination or medical test of all contract labour deployed under this Contract, to the extent applicable under Section 6(1)(c) of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, and the Rules & Regulati ons, notification and directions applicable to the establishment. Such examin ation shall be conducted by a qualified medical practitioner or an authorized medical facility, as applicable under law. The Contractor shall maintain prope r records of such medical examination and furnish copies of the medical fitne ss certificates and other relevant documents to Principal Employer, as and w hen required, subject to applicable laws relating to confidentiality and protec tion of medical information. The Contractor shall ensure that any employee found medically unfit for the assigned work is not deployed in such work unless and until the applicable m edical and statutory requirements are duly satisfied. • Contractor/Service Provider shall ensure that appointment letters are issue d to every contract labour deployed by it at buyer’s premise for performance of work under this contract, in accordance with the OSH Code, before permit ting such contract labour to commence work under establishment of the Prin cipal employer. The appointment letter shall specify, inter alia, the name and designation of the contract labour, nature of duties, date of engagement, pla ce of deployment, wages and other applicable service conditions, in accorda nce with the applicable labour laws and statutory requirements in force from time to time. A model format for the same is enclosed as Annexure-I. The Contractor shall maintain proper records of all such appointment letters and provide copies thereof to the Principal Employer, as and when required, for v erification and compliance purposes. Issuance of appointment letters by the Contractor shall not, by itself, create any employer–employee relationship be tween the Principal Employer and the contract labour. Any failure by the Con tractor to comply with this clause shall constitute a breach of the Contract an d shall render the Contractor liable to appropriate contractual action in accor dance with the terms and conditions of the Contract, without Prejudice to any other rights or remedies available to the Principal Employer under applicable law. • Contractor shall issue detailed wage slips to all contract labour either in ele ctronic or physical form in accordance with applicable labour laws before or at the time of wage disbursement. Such Wage Slips must contain details suc h as the wage period, rate of wages and deductions made, etc. in accordanc e with applicable labour laws. A model format of wage slip is enclosed as Ann exure-II. • Contractor / Supplier shall ensure that the deployed manpower complies wi th site rules, safety and security instructions. • The Contractor shall not remove, discontinue or replace any contract labou r deployed/engaged for the performance of work under this Contract without obtaining the prior written permission of the Principal Employer, except in ca ses of emergency or other circumstances where immediate action is necessa ry under applicable law. The Contractor may request such removal or replac ement on reasonable and justifiable grounds, including misconduct, unsatisf actory performance, continued absenteeism, incapacity to perform the assig

ned duties, safety or security concerns, or any other legitimate administrativ e or operational reason. Any removal, replacement or discontinuance of depl oyment shall be carried out in compliance with applicable labour laws, the te rms of employment of the concerned contract labour, and the provisions of t his Contract. The grant of permission by the Principal Employer shall not abs olve the Contractor of its statutory or contractual obligations towards the con cerned contract labour. • The Principal Employer shall have the right, for reasons to be recorded in w riting, to require the Contractor to remove from the premises of the Principal Employer any contract labour deployed by the Contractor who is found to be negligent, in disciplined, involved in misconduct, incompetent, medically unfi t for the assigned duties, in violation of applicable safety requirements, or wh ose conduct or continued deployment is considered prejudicial to the safety, security, discipline or operational requirements of the establishment. Upon r eceipt of such written direction, the Contractor shall promptly withdraw and r eplace the concerned contract labour with suitable personnel, at its own cost, without any additional financial liability to the Principal Employer and without adversely affecting the continuity or quality of the contracted service s. The Contractor shall ensure that such replacement personnel possess the r equisite qualifications, experience, training and statutory clearances, wherev er applicable. No direction issued by the Principal Employer under this clause shall, by itself, be construed as creating an employer–employee relationship between the Principal Employer and any contract labour. In cases involving a n immediate threat to life, safety, security or property, the Principal Employe r may require the immediate removal of the concerned contract labour from the premises, followed by written confirmation of the direction, wherev er practicable. The exercise of this right shall be without prejudice to the Prin cipal Employer's other rights and remedies under the Contract and applicabl e law. • Contractor / Supplier shall ensure compliance with statutory provisions of w orking hours and weekly-off. The Contractor shall ensure that all deployed pe rsonnel are provided weekly-off in accordance with applicable labor laws and statutory provisions. No contract labor shall be deployed beyond permissible hours without written authorization of Buyer. • In case contract labor is deployed on designated weekly off day, the contra ctor shall be solely liable for payment of overtime wages and / or grant comp ensatory leave strictly in accordance with applicable law and contractor shall solely responsible for maintenance of relevant records. The Buyer is neither r esponsible for monitoring / administrating the deployment of manpower nor shall the Buyer be responsible for reimbursement of overtime, paid by the co ntractor to deployed manpower due to deployment on designated weekly off day. • The Contractor/Service Provider shall ensure uninterrupted availability of t he required manpower at the designated work location throughout all days o n which the services are required as per the Contract. • Notwithstanding the requirement for daily and continuous deployment of th e requisite manpower, no individual contract labor shall be deployed in contr avention of the applicable provisions of labor codes. • The Contractor/Service Provider shall at its own cost and responsibility, dep loy adequate reliever/substitute manpower to provide service to Buyer / SPM N as per the Contract and applicable labor codes.

• Scrutiny of manpower will be done by HR department. • Payment / Reimbursement clause – “(i) The Buyer shall make the payment to service provider within 45 days fro m the date of receipt of invoice, attendance sheet, logbook, service feedbac k, documentary proofs for wages/PF/ESI/EDLI, etc. payments.
